heading: Limitation on indemnification
lead: Funds appropriated to the Department of Defense may not be used to indemnify any person under the terms of a contract entered into under this chapter—

tree.text: for any amount paid or due by any person to the United States for any liability arising under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986; or
to pay any attorneys’ fees in connection with such contract.

notes.heading: References in Text
notes.text: The Internal Revenue Code of 1986, referred to in par. (1), is classified generally to Title 26, Internal Revenue Code.

notes.heading: Codification
notes.text: The text of par. (2) of subsec. (c) of section 2401 of this title, which was transferred to this section and amended by Pub. L. 116–283, § 1825(c), was based on Pub. L. 98–525, title XII, § 1232(a)(1)(C), Oct. 19, 1984, 98 Stat. 2600; Pub. L. 103–35, title II, § 201(c)(6), May 31, 1993, 107 Stat. 98; Pub. L. 104–106, div. A, title XV, § 1503(a)(21), Feb. 10, 1996, 110 Stat. 512.

notes.heading: Amendments
notes.text: 2021—Pub. L. 116–283, § 1825(c), transferred par. (2) of section 2401(c) of this title to this section, struck out par. (2) designation at beginning, substituted “this chapter” for “this section” in introductory provisions, and redesignated subpars. (A) and (B) of such former par. (2) as pars. (1) and (2), respectively.

notes.heading: Effective Date
notes.text: Section and amendment by Pub. L. 116–283 effective Jan. 1, 2022, with additional provisions for delayed implementation and applicability of existing law, see section 1801(d) of Pub. L. 116–283, set out as an Effective Date of 2021 Amendment note preceding section 3001 of this title.

sourceCredit: (Added and amended Pub. L. 116–283, div. A, title XVIII, § 1825(a), (c), Jan. 1, 2021, 134 Stat. 4206.)
